positions.claim: Forward deployed engineering and product engineering should be the same role, with the same hiring bar and reporting structure, rather than separate organizations.
Now that AI coding tools are good, the scarce engineering skill is restraint — not building the fast one-off solution.
An agent built as a pile of customer-specific prompts and patches is too brittle and bad for both vendor and customer.
Enterprise product asks recur across customers with high regularity, so every customer-specific solution should be architected for the next four customers.
AI coding has shifted engineering effort toward up-front requirements gathering and alignment rather than starting to build immediately.
Success metrics and channels should be agreed in writing during the earliest deal conversations.
Staffing the same industry-expert group across customers in a vertical produces faster ramp-up and more credibility than generalist staffing.
In enterprise deployments you should deliberately narrow initial scope to prove value fast, then expand, rather than accepting the full kitchen-sink scope.
Forward deployed people accumulate cross-customer domain expertise that makes them advisors, and this expertise is routinely underrated.
Any task a Decagon engineer has to do manually is a signal that a product capability is missing and should be upstreamed.
Building custom integrations one at a time does not scale; after about 25 of them a self-serve path was the correct investment.
Decagon's speed on customer asks, advisor positioning, and productization of custom work are the three reasons it won its market position.
The kind of forward deployment required differs substantially by enterprise size and by vertical.
Companies at 500 people must design the deployment system itself, whereas at 50 people ad hoc knowledge sharing was sufficient.
